newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: CLOUD SEEDING SOUGHT FOR PARCHED PHILIPPINE FARMS.
newsitem.headline: CLOUD SEEDING SOUGHT FOR PARCHED PHILIPPINE FARMS.

text.p: Rice and corn farmers in the Philippines, who suffered planting delays due to sparse rains in recent weeks, have flooded the government with requests for cloud seeding, officials said on Tuesday.
"Even the farmers' standing crops have been affected by lack of water," said Wilfredo Cabeson, chief of the cloud seeding operations of the Bureau of Soils and Water Management.
Cabeson told reporters the affected farmers were from the Cagayan Valley and Bicol regions in northern Luzon island and South Cotabato in southern Mindanao island.
He said his department was set to conduct a 40-hour cloud seeding trip in the Cagayan Valley region to save the 158,000 hectares of corn farms affected by the dry spell.
Cabeson said his department was also finalising plans to conduct another cloud seeding in the Bicol region, particularly in the rice farms of Camarines Sur province.
He said his department has been conducting cloud seeding operations over rice and corn growing areas in the country due to lack of water for irrigation.
The Philippine weather bureau said water levels in the country's five major dams have dipped below normal levels due to below-average rainfall in recent weeks.
In an advisory early this month, it said most parts of the country experienced little rain between April and July this year due to fewer-than-usual cyclones.

Weather experts attributed the dry weather to El Nino, a weather condition caused by warming of water in the Pacific ocean which creates drought in some areas and heavier-than-normal rainfall in others.
The Philippines was supposed to be at the height of its rainy season now, which normally starts April and ends in September.

Environment Secretary Victor Ramos said a government committee on the sustainable use of water resources had requested budget funding of 80 million pesos to buy giant plastic sheets which are to be used for impounding water.
